answer_html:
Definition

MVC (Model–View–Controller) is a design pattern that splits a component into three parts: the Model (data), the View (display) and the Controller (user input).

Key points

  • Model: stores data/state (e.g. ButtonModel, ListModel, TableModel).
  • View: shows the model on screen.
  • Controller: handles user input and updates the model.
  • Swing joins View and Controller into a UI delegate (Model–Delegate design).
  • Advantages: change the look without changing data; same data in many views; easier to maintain.

Figure

User --input--> [Controller] --updates--> [Model] --notifies--> [View] --shows--> User
